newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St George sees flatter 96/97 result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St George sees flatter 96/97 result.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd said on Tuesday it expects a flatter result in the year to September 30, 1997 due to intense competition in the Australian banking sector, which will also put pressure on margins.

"While the board anticipates earnings to remain at a satisfactory level, it acknowledges that competition within the banking sector will remain intense, resulting in additional pressures on margins and a flatter result in 1997," it said.
St George earlier reported a net profit before preference dividends of A$148.3 million for the year, a rise of 9.4 percent.

The bank said demand for housing is expected to grow as the impact of lower interest rates begin to stimulate the market, with volume growth offsetting some of the imapct of reduced spreads in this market.
"Interest spreads which have remained stable during the year, are expected to contract in the ensuring year as the impact of recent reductions in l;ending rates take effect," St George said.

St George announced last month an agreed A$2.65 billion merger with fellow Sydney-based regional bank Advance Bank Australia Ltd, which would give the combined bank, to be called St George, assets of about A$40 billion.

It said the planned merger, which would give the bank a larger more diversified asset base, together with new products in life insurance and its home loan products will ensure that St George remains an effective competitor.
The bank said the insurance business is expected to start in the first half of 1997. It also said the introduction of new technology will assist in controlling operating costs.
St George shares closed 21 cents lower at A$8.66 on Monday.
